from tunepad.constants import *

# BLUE HOUR CHORDS
# this cell creates the harmony of my song
# harmony is the chords underneath the melody

# I use TunePad constants so I can write note names like C4 and Eb4
# this is easier for me to understand than only using numbers


# INTRO CHORDS
# I use 7th and 9th chords because they sound richer and smoother
# this fits the dreamy R&B feeling of Blue Hour

intro_chords = [
    [C4, Eb4, G4, Bb4, D5],   # Cm9
    [Ab3, C4, Eb4, G4],       # Abmaj7
    [F3, Ab3, C4, Eb4, G4],   # Fm9
    [G3, B3, D4, F4]          # G7
]


# VERSE CHORDS
# these are slightly simpler than the intro chords

verse_chords = [
    [C4, Eb4, G4, Bb4],       # Cm7
    [Ab3, C4, Eb4, G4],       # Abmaj7
    [F3, Ab3, C4, Eb4],       # Fm7
    [G3, B3, D4, F4]          # G7
]


# CHORUS CHORDS
# I change the progression in the chorus
# this stops the whole song from sounding like one repeated loop

chorus_chords = [
    [Ab3, C4, Eb4, G4],
    [Bb3, D4, F4, A4],
    [C4, Eb4, G4, Bb4, D5],
    [G3, B3, D4, F4]
]


# INTRO
# range(2) means repeat the whole intro progression 2 times
# a loop is better than copying and pasting the same chords again

for i in range(2):

    # this loop goes through each chord in the list
    for chord in intro_chords:

        # playNote() plays the notes
        # because "chord" contains several notes, they play together
        # beats=4 means the chord lasts for 4 beats
        # velocity controls how strong the sound is
        # sustain lets the chord ring a little longer
        # I use low velocity because the intro should feel soft and dreamy

        playNote(chord, beats=4, velocity=38, sustain=1)


# VERSE
for i in range(4):

    for chord in verse_chords:

        # slightly stronger than the intro
        # this slowly builds the song

        playNote(chord, beats=4, velocity=44, sustain=1)


# CHORUS
for i in range(4):

    for chord in chorus_chords:

        # higher velocity makes the chorus feel fuller
        # but I still keep it smooth because it is R&B

        playNote(chord, beats=4, velocity=50, sustain=1)


# OUTRO
# I return to the intro chords
# this helps the song finish with the same Blue Hour mood

for i in range(2):

    for chord in intro_chords:

        # softer again for the ending

        playNote(chord, beats=4, velocity=34, sustain=1)

from tunepad.constants import *

# BLUE HOUR - BASS
# this cell creates the low part of the song
# bass supports the chords and makes the R&B groove feel deeper


# INTRO
# rest() means silence
# I leave the first 16 beats empty so the piano starts by itself
# this makes the beginning feel more atmospheric

rest(16)


# these notes match the main roots of my chords

intro_bass = [C2, Ab1, F1, G1]


for note in intro_bass:

    # beats=2 makes the bass note longer
    # velocity=42 keeps the intro bass soft

    playNote(note, beats=2, velocity=42)

    # I use rest() to leave space between bass notes
    # space helps the bass feel relaxed instead of too busy

    rest(2)


# VERSE
for i in range(4):

    # main C bass note

    playNote(C2, beats=1.5, velocity=58)

    rest(1)

    # G is a passing note
    # I added passing notes so the bass has some movement
    # instead of only playing one note for each chord

    playNote(G2, beats=0.5, velocity=44)

    rest(1)


    # Ab bass

    playNote(Ab1, beats=1.5, velocity=56)

    rest(1)

    playNote(Eb2, beats=0.5, velocity=43)

    rest(1)


    # F bass

    playNote(F1, beats=1.5, velocity=58)

    rest(1)

    playNote(C2, beats=0.5, velocity=44)

    rest(1)


    # G bass

    playNote(G1, beats=1.5, velocity=60)

    # B leads back toward C
    # this makes the loop connect more smoothly

    playNote(B1, beats=0.5, velocity=42)

    rest(2)


# CHORUS
for i in range(4):

    # the chorus bass is stronger
    # this helps the chorus feel bigger than the verse

    playNote(Ab1, beats=2, velocity=62)
    playNote(Eb2, beats=1, velocity=46)
    rest(1)

    playNote(Bb1, beats=2, velocity=60)
    playNote(F2, beats=1, velocity=46)
    rest(1)

    playNote(C2, beats=2, velocity=64)
    playNote(G2, beats=1, velocity=48)
    rest(1)

    playNote(G1, beats=2, velocity=62)
    playNote(B1, beats=0.5, velocity=44)
    rest(1.5)


# OUTRO
# the bass becomes simple again
# this helps the song calm down at the end

for note in [C2, Ab1, F1, G1]:

    playNote(note, beats=2, velocity=38)

    rest(2)


# final space with no bass

rest(16)

# BLUE HOUR - KICK
# this cell creates the low drum pulse of the song
# the kick is important for giving the track an R&B groove


# INTRO
# no kick for the first 32 beats
# I want the song to start softly before the full beat comes in

rest(32)


# VERSE
for i in range(16):

    # note 0 is the kick in my 808 Drumkit
    # the first kick is stronger

    playNote(0, beats=0.5, velocity=65)

    rest(1)

    # second kick is softer
    # changing velocity makes the beat feel less robotic

    playNote(0, beats=0.5, velocity=48)

    rest(0.5)

    # extra kick near the end
    # this makes the rhythm more syncopated
    # instead of having a very basic straight beat

    playNote(0, beats=0.5, velocity=58)

    rest(1)


# CHORUS
for i in range(16):

    # stronger kick pattern makes the chorus feel bigger

    playNote(0, beats=0.5, velocity=70)

    rest(0.5)

    playNote(0, beats=0.5, velocity=52)

    rest(1)

    playNote(0, beats=0.5, velocity=64)

    rest(1)


# OUTRO
# I remove the kick completely
# this brings the calm feeling back

rest(32)

# BLUE HOUR - SNARE
# this cell creates the backbeat of my R&B rhythm
# the snare helps make the beat easier to feel


# INTRO
# no snare at the start

rest(32)


# VERSE
for i in range(16):

    # rest() controls when the snare enters
    # I do not want every drum sound playing together

    rest(1)

    # note 2 is the snare sound
    # beats=0.5 keeps the snare short
    # velocity=48 keeps it soft

    playNote(2, beats=0.5, velocity=48)

    rest(1.5)

    # second snare is slightly stronger
    # small velocity changes make it feel more natural

    playNote(2, beats=0.5, velocity=52)

    rest(0.5)


# CHORUS
for i in range(16):

    rest(1)

    # louder snare during the chorus

    playNote(2, beats=0.5, velocity=58)

    rest(1)

    playNote(2, beats=0.5, velocity=60)

    rest(1)


# OUTRO
# drums disappear again

rest(32)

# New TunePad cell
from tunepad.constants import *

# BLUE HOUR - MELODY
# this cell creates the main emotional melody of the song

# I use Crystal Organ because it has a soft and dreamy sound
# this fits the calm and slightly melancholic feeling of Blue Hour

# repeat the melody 8 times
for i in range(8):

    # playNote() plays one note at a time
    # beats controls how long each note lasts
    # I use different beat lengths so the melody sounds less robotic

    playNote(G4, beats=1, velocity=40)

    # shorter note adds movement
    playNote(Bb4, beats=0.5, velocity=38)

    # longer note creates a more emotional feeling
    playNote(C5, beats=1.5, velocity=44)

    # rest() creates silence
    # I use space because slow R&B melodies should not feel too crowded
    rest(0.5)

    playNote(Bb4, beats=0.5, velocity=38)
    playNote(G4, beats=1, velocity=40)
    playNote(Eb4, beats=1, velocity=36)

    # another pause makes the melody feel relaxed
    rest(0.5)

    # small response phrase
    playNote(F4, beats=0.5, velocity=38)
    playNote(G4, beats=0.5, velocity=42)
    playNote(Bb4, beats=1, velocity=40)

    rest(1)

    # longer ending note finishes the phrase
    playNote(G4, beats=2, velocity=42)

    # space before the melody repeats
    rest(1)

from tunepad.constants import *

# BLUE HOUR - AD LIB
# this is a second small melody
# it answers the main melody instead of playing all the time

# I use Musicbox because it sounds different from the Crystal Organ
# this helps the two melody layers stay separate


# INTRO
# no ad lib during the intro
# I want the song to slowly build

rest(32)


# VERSE
for i in range(4):

    # wait first
    # the ad lib only fills empty spaces

    rest(4)

    # small high note

    playNote(Eb5, beats=0.5, velocity=30)

    rest(0.5)

    # second response note

    playNote(C5, beats=0.5, velocity=28)

    # longer ending note

    playNote(Bb4, beats=1, velocity=32)

    # lots of silence
    # I do this because too many notes would make the R&B track crowded

    rest(9.5)


# CHORUS
for i in range(4):

    # the ad lib becomes slightly more active in the chorus

    rest(2)

    playNote(Eb5, beats=0.5, velocity=34)

    rest(0.5)

    playNote(C5, beats=0.5, velocity=32)

    playNote(Bb4, beats=0.5, velocity=30)

    rest(4)

    # higher response note

    playNote(G5, beats=0.5, velocity=36)

    playNote(F5, beats=0.5, velocity=34)

    playNote(Eb5, beats=1, velocity=32)

    rest(6)


# OUTRO
# only a few quiet notes at the end

rest(16)

playNote(Eb5, beats=1, velocity=26)

rest(3)

playNote(C5, beats=1, velocity=24)

rest(3)

playNote(Bb4, beats=2, velocity=22)
